decisions.reason: Changing the webhook query's contract-address filter does not alter the approved migration data policy or deployment strategy.
The filtered contract address does not change the rule that only finalized successful mints may be reported as owned NFTs.
The source configures contract-event retrieval but establishes no change to prize-pool or platform-statistics accuracy requirements.
The webhook filter update does not change the required referral, ticket, commission, or earnings reporting semantics.
Although the Discord structure mentioned a future system-log webhook, the source only changes a separate production contract-event query and does not change the community-server requirement.
The contract address used for event filtering is unrelated to remediation of the production-domain malicious-site warning.
The webhook query update does not change NFT-holder eligibility, Lit Protocol configuration, or the ownership-check behavior.
The contract-event filter has no semantic effect on the support form's placement, fields, purposes, or navigation entry.
The source contains no decision to revise FAQ copy or its documented product topics.
Updating a contract-event query address does not change the manual redemption mode or eligibility-window visibility of the prize claim control.
The webhook filter update does not change the Transak provider, fiat methods, wallet provisioning, mint destination, or deferred lifecycle.
The source does not change the required USDC wallet-mint behavior or payment asset; it only updates event-query filtering.
